answer: An applicant books one shale bed and stakes a 70-credit bond. It sows ten lotus kernels and logs the bed, date, and kernel count. An auditor counts live sprouts against the kernel count and checks roots anchored in bed soil; a short count, loose root, or duplicate bed filing burns the bond. A bed costs 34 credits; the kth bed costs 34+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5029 and 1000 fakes pay 2,531,500 plus 70,000 locked. A genuine applicant spends 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean count. A rented-sprout ring fails: transplanted lotus sprouts fail the root check with severed roots.
